title: Session-burst adaptive batching simulator and p95 heatmap probe
creator: Marco Chen
description: Build and validate a hybrid session burst simulator that exercises continuous batching + queueing behavior under mixed workloads (interactive short sessions, long streaming sessions, and background bulk requests). Unlike previous arrival-harnesses, this work models session stickiness (session-affinity with KV cache warm/cold transitions), ON/OFF bursty arrivals, and per-session priority demotion. The simulator must output per-token throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, batch-size distributions, queue-length heatmaps, and regression flags for automated CI. The goal is to identify configuration sweet spots (max batch deadline, per-session demotion threshold, per GPU concurrency) that avoid tail amplification while preserving tokens/sec during bursts.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay 3 workload profiles: interactive-heavy, mixed-tenant blend, and long-stream dominated, with configurable ON/OFF burst parameters
Heatmap viz showing p95 latency vs concurrency and batch_deadline validated against Prometheus traces for at least 5 canonical runs
Automated regression detector flags 10%+ p95 regressions and posts artifacts to CI (build job) with links to the relevant run and dashboard
Recommended runtime knobs (batch_deadline, max_batch_size, per-session demotion window) documented and can be applied via a config toggle for A/B testing
Benchmarks reproducible: docker image + run script producing artifact tarball with metrics and raw traces
tasks: Design simulator API and config schema (profiles, session affinity parameters)
Implement arrival generator: Poisson + ON/OFF burst mode + stickiness token model
Wire simulator to runtime test harness to record traces (token-level timestamps, batch ids, kv cache hits)
Build Grafana heatmap dashboards and CI regression job that uploads artifacts
Run baseline runs against runtime-1.20 and runtime-1.21 for comparison
Write PR with README, example configs, and sanity test

findings_summary: Preliminary runs show a non-linear p95 amplification for interactive-heavy workloads when burst_factor >= 3 and batch_deadline > 12ms. Key drivers: head-of-line blocking caused by long streaming requests coalescing with short sessions, and KV-cold sessions that anchor batches and delay many short requests. Tokens/sec remains acceptable, but tail latency degrades by 30-80% depending on config. Lowering batch_deadline to 6-8ms or enabling per-session demotion (move long sessions to demoted queue after 1s) reduces p95 by ~40% with 5-10% tokens/sec loss.
decisions: Prototype per-session demotion: long sessions are queued into a demoted FIFO after N tokens or T ms; demoted queue gets smaller max_batch and stricter deadline
Expose batch_deadline and per-session demotion parameters as runtime toggles for canary experiments in Dedicated clusters
Add head-of-line blocking metric and include it in regression detector features
risks: Simulator complexity might diverge from production scheduling edge cases (kernel-level preemption, GPU memory pressure)
False positives in regression detector due to non-deterministic arrival seeding; need seeding and monotonic clocks
Applying strict demotion could increase cost per token for long-running streams if not tuned
